dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a natural number n, this is the type of real n by n matrices, represented as functions Fin n → Fin n → Real.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The universally quantified A is a square real matrix with n rows and n columns.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a natural number n, this is the type of real vectors indexed by Fin n, represented as functions Fin n → Real.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The vectors b, xHat, and the vector perturbation deltaB each have exactly n real coordinates.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: A matrix A satisfies this predicate exactly when its associated matrix-vector map x ↦ Ax is bijective.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The proposition assumes that A acts bijectively on the real n-dimensional vector space; equivalently in this finite square setting, A is invertible.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the real number ‖b - A xHat‖₂ divided by ‖A‖_F ‖xHat‖₂ + ‖b‖₂.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It specifies the claimed least feasible relative perturbation size.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a real epsilon, this predicate holds when there exist a real n by n matrix deltaA and a real n-vector deltaB such that (A + deltaA)xHat = b + deltaB, ‖deltaA‖_F ≤ epsilon ‖A‖_F, and ‖deltaB‖₂ ≤ epsilon ‖b‖₂.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It defines the set of feasible common relative backward-error bounds whose least element is asserted by the conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the Frobenius norm of a real square matrix: ‖A‖_F = sqrt(Σ_i Σ_j A_ij²).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It measures both the size of A and the admissible matrix perturbation deltaA.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef007
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is ordinary matrix-vector multiplication, with (Ax)_i = Σ_j A_ij x_j over all j in Fin n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It defines the bijectivity hypothesis, the residual, and the perturbed equation.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef008
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the residual vector b - Ax.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Applied to xHat, its Euclidean norm is the numerator of the claimed minimum.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef009
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the Euclidean norm of a real n-vector: ‖x‖₂ = sqrt(Σ_i x_i²).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It measures the residual, xHat, b, and the vector perturbation deltaB.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin
dependency_coverage.meaning: Fin n is the finite type of natural-number indices strictly less than n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes all matrix and vector coordinates range over exactly n indices.

dependency_coverage.name: IsLeast
dependency_coverage.meaning: IsLeast S a means that a belongs to S and is a lower bound of S, namely a ≤ s for every s in S.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The conclusion asserts both feasibility of the displayed quotient and its inequality against every other feasible epsilon, so the minimum is attained.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat
dependency_coverage.meaning: Nat is the type of natural numbers, including zero.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The dimension n is universally quantified over all finite dimensions, including n = 0.

dependency_coverage.name: Ne
dependency_coverage.meaning: Ne a b means that a = b is false.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The hypothesis Ne b 0 says that b is not the identically zero vector.

dependency_coverage.name: OfNat.ofNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: This retrieves the value assigned to a numeral by an OfNat instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets the literal 0 in the hypothesis b ≠ 0 as the zero vector.

dependency_coverage.name: Pi.instZero
dependency_coverage.meaning: The zero of a function type is the pointwise zero function.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The zero vector in b ≠ 0 has every coordinate equal to the real number zero.

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real is the type of real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: All entries, coordinates, norms, perturbation bounds, and candidate epsilon values are real.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLE
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies the usual order relation ≤ on the real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instZero
dependency_coverage.meaning: This supplies the usual real number zero.

dependency_coverage.name: Zero.toOfNat0
dependency_coverage.meaning: This makes the numeral 0 denote the zero supplied by a Zero instance.

dependency_coverage.name: setOf
dependency_coverage.meaning: Given a predicate p, setOf p is the set of all values satisfying p.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It forms the set of real epsilon values for which suitable perturbations exist.

dependency_coverage.name: And
dependency_coverage.meaning: And P Q is logical conjunction, requiring both propositions.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It combines the perturbed equation with both norm bounds, expands bijectivity into injectivity and surjectivity, and expands leastness into membership and the lower-bound property.

dependency_coverage.name: DivInvMonoid.toDiv
dependency_coverage.meaning: This extracts a division operation from a division-and-inverse monoid structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For Real, it supplies the ordinary real division used in the displayed quotient.

dependency_coverage.name: Eq

dependency_coverage.name: Exists

dependency_coverage.name: Function.Bijective
dependency_coverage.meaning: A function is bijective exactly when it is both injective and surjective.

dependency_coverage.name: HAdd.hAdd

dependency_coverage.name: HDiv.hDiv

dependency_coverage.name: LE.le
dependency_coverage.meaning: This extracts the binary ≤ relation from an LE instance.

dependency_coverage.name: Matrix
dependency_coverage.meaning: Matrix m n alpha is definitionally the function type m → n → alpha.

dependency_coverage.name: Matrix.add
dependency_coverage.meaning: Matrix addition is inherited from pointwise addition of functions.

dependency_coverage.name: Pi.instAdd

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAdd

binders: Let n be an arbitrary natural number.
Let A = (A_ij) be an arbitrary real n by n matrix.
Let b and xHat be arbitrary vectors in R^n.
hypotheses: The map R^n → R^n given by x ↦ Ax is bijective.
The vector b is not the zero vector.
conclusions: Define eta = ‖b - A xHat‖₂ / (‖A‖_F ‖xHat‖₂ + ‖b‖₂). Then there exist a real n by n matrix deltaA and a real n-vector deltaB such that (A + deltaA)xHat = b + deltaB, ‖deltaA‖_F ≤ eta ‖A‖_F, and ‖deltaB‖₂ ≤ eta ‖b‖₂.
For every real epsilon for which there exist deltaA and deltaB satisfying (A + deltaA)xHat = b + deltaB, ‖deltaA‖_F ≤ epsilon ‖A‖_F, and ‖deltaB‖₂ ≤ epsilon ‖b‖₂, one has eta ≤ epsilon.
mathematical_definitions: The index set is Fin n, corresponding to {0, ..., n - 1} when n > 0.
Matrix-vector multiplication is (Ax)_i = Σ_j A_ij x_j.
The residual is r = b - A xHat.
For a vector v, ‖v‖₂ = sqrt(Σ_i v_i²).
For a matrix M, ‖M‖_F = sqrt(Σ_i Σ_j M_ij²).
A real epsilon is feasible exactly when there are perturbations deltaA and deltaB satisfying the exact perturbed equation and both relative norm bounds with the same epsilon.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every finite dimension, every bijective real square matrix A, every nonzero right-hand side b, and every candidate vector xHat, the smallest common relative normwise perturbation bound epsilon for which xHat exactly solves a perturbed system (A + deltaA)xHat = b + deltaB is exactly ‖b - A xHat‖₂ divided by ‖A‖_F ‖xHat‖₂ + ‖b‖₂, where matrix perturbations are measured in the Frobenius norm and vector perturbations in the Euclidean norm.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The dimension n is allowed to be zero, but then every vector is the zero vector, so the hypothesis b ≠ 0 is impossible and the implication is vacuous.
Only square real matrices are covered, and A is required to act bijectively; singular and rectangular systems are not covered.
The right-hand side b must be nonzero. There is no nonzero assumption on xHat.
The denominator is positive under b ≠ 0 because ‖b‖₂ > 0, so the quotient does not encounter a zero denominator under the hypotheses.

The feasible-set parameter epsilon ranges over all real numbers; nonnegativity is not an explicit assumption. Nevertheless, no negative epsilon is feasible because ‖deltaB‖₂ is nonnegative while epsilon ‖b‖₂ would be negative.

The matrix bound is normwise relative in the Frobenius norm, and the vector bound is normwise relative in the Euclidean norm. No componentwise, structured, sparsity-preserving, or sign constraints are imposed on the perturbations.
The same epsilon bounds both relative perturbations, corresponding to the maximum of the two relative sizes rather than their sum.
The perturbed equation is exact and uses the fixed vector xHat; the proposition does not assume that xHat solves the original system.
Leastness means an attained minimum, not merely an infimum, and the conclusion itself asserts that perturbations attaining the displayed value exist.
No uniqueness of the minimizing perturbations is asserted.
No floating-point arithmetic model, rounding process, algorithm, condition number, or provenance of xHat is encoded.
